results.note: BIA Pine Ridge Agency page (fetched 2026-10-09): tribe 'boasts an enrollment of 46,855 members'. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: reservation 'consists of approximately 2.1 million acres' and occupies Oglala Lakota, Jackson and Bennett counties. Evidence verbatim.
Tribe's History & Culture page: 'The Rosebud Sioux Tribe, more properly known as Sicangu Lakota Oyate, or Burnt Thigh People'. Evidence verbatim.

Evidence verbatim and 20 communities supported, but the same page gives two different land figures (heritage text '922,759 acres' vs General Information 'Land Area: 882,416 acres'). Dropped the acreage; kept communities and headquarters (General Information also lists 'Tribal headquarters: Rosebud, South Dakota').
results.text: The Rosebud Reservation takes in 20 communities, and the tribal headquarters is in the community of Rosebud, South Dakota.
results.evidence: The tribal headquarters is located in the community of Rosebud

results.note: Misattribution: the page says the Lakota overall (about 70,000 today) have approximately 1/3 still speaking their ancestral language; it is not a figure for Rosebud members. Rewritten to match. Evidence verbatim.
results.text: The tribe's history page says the Lakota number about 70,000 today, and that about a third of them still speak their ancestral language.
results.evidence: approximately 1/3 still speak their ancestral language

results.note: ND Indian Affairs Commission page: 'English is widely spoken, while Lakota is also used and actively being revitalized.' The page does not say Lakota is in daily use; removed that overstatement. Evidence verbatim.
results.text: At Standing Rock, English is widely spoken, and the Lakota language is also used and is being actively revitalized.
results.evidence: Lakota is also used and actively being revitalized

results.note: Same page: Chairman, Vice-Chairman, a Secretary and 14 council members (8 district, 6 at-large); 'Positions are elected by the tribal members and serve a term of four years.' Evidence verbatim.
Tribe's About page: Yanktonai live primarily on the North Dakota portion; 'Today the Lakota at Standing Rock live predominantly in communities located on the South Dakota portion'. Evidence verbatim.
BIA Cheyenne River Agency page: tribe 'consisting predominantly of the Minneconjou, SiHaSapa, Oohenumpa, and Itazipco bands of the Lakota'. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'Governing body is a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer and fifteen council members'; tribal office address and agency headquarters in Eagle Butte. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: '1,450,644 trust acres in Ziebach and Dewey County in central South Dakota' (plus parts of other counties). Evidence verbatim.
SWO homepage: 'Our reservation boundaries span 7 counties, 2 in North Dakota and 5 in South Dakota.' Evidence verbatim.
SWO homepage: 'We have 14,000+ tribal members throughout the US and abroad in the Armed Forces.' Evidence verbatim.

SWO homepage says it represents the Dakota people of the Sisitunwan-Wahpetunwan Oyate; its Seven Districts menu lists Dakota names (Iyakaptapi, Canowanasapi, Toka Nuwan, Heipa, Bde Hdakinyan, Kaksiza Hanska, Ateyapi Tipi). Evidence verbatim.
ND Indian Affairs Commission page: 'both English and the Dakota language (specifically the Eastern Dakota dialect) are spoken'. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: northeastern ND, primarily Benson County, about 405 square miles or about 259,000 acres. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'Cankdeska Cikana Community College offers 12 programs for associate degrees and certificates.' Evidence verbatim.
SMSC Our History timeline: 'On November 28, 1969, the Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community formally became a federally recognized Indian tribe'. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'We are still here and continue to live our traditional Dakota lifeways that will be passed through future generations.' Evidence verbatim; the paraphrase is in the researcher's own words.
SMSC homepage: 'Following the Dakota tradition of helping others, the SMSC donates millions of dollars each year to other tribes, organizations, and local governments.' Evidence verbatim.

mn.gov blocks scripted fetches (bot check), but WebFetch of the page (title 'Miskwaagamiiwi-Zaagaiganing / Red Lake Nation', Minnesota Indian Affairs Council) returned 'All land is held in common by the members of the Band.' Evidence verbatim.
Red Lake Nation homepage: 'The tribal government has full sovereignty over the reservation, subject only to the federal government.' Evidence verbatim.

Page (via WebFetch) says 'English is a second language to many Red Lake members middle-aged and older including some on the Tribal Council' and 'Ojibwe is spoken and/or understood by many others.' It does not say Ojibwe is their first language; rewritten to the page's own claims. Evidence verbatim.
results.text: English is a second language for many Red Lake members who are middle-aged and older, including some on the Tribal Council, and many others speak or understand Ojibwe.
results.evidence: English is a second language to many Red Lake members

results.note: Mille Lacs Band homepage: 'Our Band has a three-branch division-of-powers form of government, with an Executive Branch, Legislative Branch and Judicial Branch.' Evidence verbatim.
Same page: homelands of three Districts throughout East Central Minnesota; 'self-governing Indian nation of nearly 4800 enrolled Band Members'. Evidence verbatim.
ND Indian Affairs Commission page: 'Languages: English, Ojibwe, and Michif (language is a mix of French, Ojibwe, & Cree)'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'a total estimate of 33,276 members enrolled (7/10/24)'. The page belongs to the state commission and does not say the band made the estimate; reworded neutrally. Evidence verbatim.
results.text: As of July 2024, an estimated 33,276 members were enrolled in the Turtle Mountain Band.
results.evidence: a total estimate of 33,276 members enrolled

results.note: The page text is the state commission's own and is not attributed to the band, so 'the band describes' is unsupported. Page: over the past two centuries a blended culture with Ojibwe and Metis influences created 'a unique heritage that is found nowhere else but here.' Reworded. Evidence verbatim.
results.text: Over two centuries, Ojibwe and Metis influences blended at Turtle Mountain into a unique heritage found nowhere else.
results.evidence: a unique heritage that is found nowhere else but here

results.note: MHA Nation homepage: 'As of August 20, 2026, 17,825 members are currently enrolled in the Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation'. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: Tribal Business Council of six Segment Representatives and the Chairman; Segments are White Shield, Parshall, New Town, Four Bears, Mandaree and Twin Buttes. Evidence verbatim.
Same page header greets in Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara; Mandan line reads 'Ráátinitak shí’sh. It is good that you all arrived' (diacritics match). Evidence verbatim.
Blackfeet Nation homepage: 'home to the 17,321-member Blackfeet Nation'. Evidence verbatim.
Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs directory: 'Its one-and-a-half million acres are bordered on the north by Canada and on the west by Glacier National Park.' Evidence verbatim.

Page: 'There are three branches of the Blackfeet peoples-the Northern Blackfeet (Siksika), the Blood and the Piegan or Pikuni.' The page does not frame this as tradition; removed that framing. Evidence verbatim.
results.text: The Blackfeet peoples have three branches: the Northern Blackfeet (Siksika), the Blood, and the Piegan or Pikuni.
results.evidence: There are three branches of the Blackfeet

results.note: Montana directory: tribe 'is originally called "Apsaalooke," which means "children of the large-beaked bird."' Evidence verbatim.

Crow Tribe Executive Branch site: 'The Crow Constitution and By-Laws of 2001 established three branches of government, the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches.' Evidence verbatim.
Montana directory: 'The tribe call themselves "Tsis tsis'tas" (Tse-TSES-tas) which means "the beautiful people".' Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'approximately 444,000 acres in size with 99% tribal ownership', southeastern Montana. (Fast Facts on the same page rounds to 440,000; 'roughly' covers both.) Evidence verbatim.

Same page: 'Lame Deer is the tribal and government agency headquarters'; Tribal Council 'consists of members elected from each of the following districts: Ashland, Birney, Busby, Muddy, and Lame Deer.' Evidence verbatim.
Montana directory: 'home to two separate Indian nations, the Assiniboine & Sioux Tribes'; 'The Assiniboine refer to themselves as "Nakona" and the Sioux call themselves "Dakota".' Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'All members of the governing body, except the secretary-accountant are elected at-large every two years.' Evidence verbatim.
Same page: reservation is in northeastern Montana; 'It includes more than two million acres of land.' Evidence verbatim.

Page reachable (curl over https fails on a TLS renegotiation, but http and WebFetch both load 'About | Northern Arapaho Tribe'). Evidence verbatim. The page never says 'Wind River Reservation': it says the 2.2 million acre reserve lies between the Wind River Range and Owl Creek Mountains and is shared by Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho, and it names the tribe 'Northern Arapaho Tribe of Wyoming'. Rewritten to those words; the new evidence ties in the acreage.
results.text: The Northern Arapaho and the Eastern Shoshone share a 2.2 million acre reservation in Wyoming, between the Wind River Range and the Owl Creek Mountains.
results.evidence: Owl Creek Mountains, the 2.2 million acre reserve is shared

results.note: Same page: 'The Arapaho Flag was created in 1936 as a sign of respect and remembrance for the Arapaho War Veterans.' Evidence verbatim.

Same page: 'one of four groups of Arapaho who originally occupied the headwaters of the Arkansas and Platte Rivers.' Evidence verbatim. Note: the page also has leftover lorem ipsum filler text below the facts.
Tribes' Language and Culture page: 'Tsistsistas, is the Cheyenne word meaning "Human Beings" or "The People."' Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'an adult immersion Master Apprentice Program dedicated to producing functionally fluent speakers for both the Cheyenne and Arapaho languages.' Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'The Language Program offers classes throughout our communities and online for our tribal members.' Evidence verbatim.
Comanche Nation History page: 'The Tribal Council comprises all enrolled members over 18 and is the main governing body.' Evidence verbatim.
Comanche Nation Language page: mission 'to revitalize and reclaim the Comanche Language'; the page links an Online Learning resource. Evidence verbatim.
History page: 'were once a part of the Shoshone Tribe. In the late 1600s and early 1700s, we moved from our Shoshone kinsmen onto the northern Plains'. Evidence verbatim.

Kiowa Language Department page: 'Register for the credentialed Kiowa language teacher training program for 2025-2026' under 'LEARN AND TEACH THE KIOWA LANGUAGE'. as_of 2025 is right (deadline March 2025); re-check for currency. Evidence verbatim.
Kiowa Tribe homepage: 'devoted to protect its sovereignty, preserve and advocate its rich Kiowa culture and language'. Evidence verbatim.
About us page: Kiowa 'originated in the Kootenay Region of British Columbia, Canada' and the earliest written records place Kiowas 'in the northern basin of the Missouri River'. Evidence verbatim.

Cited /who-we-are now redirects to /government (title 'Government | Osage Nation', matching the cited title): 'On June 5, 2006 ... constitutional government, consisting of separate executive, legislative, and judicial branches'. Evidence verbatim.

Osage Nation homepage: the Constitution vests the Osage Minerals Council, which 'consists of eight Council members that serve as the elected governing body for the mineral affairs'. Evidence verbatim.

Government page: 'The Pawnee Business Council is the supreme governing body', subject to the Constitution and applicable federal law. Evidence verbatim.
CPN Government page: 'a federally recognized tribe of more than 38,000 Tribal citizens around the world'; footer address Shawnee, OK. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'In July 2026, CPN officially signed the articles of confederation for the Potawatomi Confederacy'. Evidence verbatim.
Same page: 'Constitution was created in 1938, amended in 1985 and again in 2007'. Evidence verbatim.

Tribal History page: 'originated in the Great Lakes area' and 'After 1846 the tribe moved to present-day Kansas'. Evidence verbatim. Note for respect review: the page frames this move as forced removal.

Page: 'The Cultural Center, Library and Museum provide an important link to the past'. 'Living link between Potawatomi people' overstates it, so the text is reworded to the page's meaning (the ceremony mention is left out on purpose). Evidence verbatim.

results.evidence: Cultural Center, Library and Museum provide an important link

Same page: the reservation is 'located in Brown and Outagamie Counties' and 'located in northeast Wisconsin'. Evidence verbatim.

Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma homepage: 'we call ourselves Baxoje (Bah Kho-je), meaning, "People of the Grey Snow."' Evidence verbatim.
